entries.input: Let $Q$ be a real $n \times n$ matrix with $QQ^{T} = I$, let $u \in \mathbb{R}^{n}$ satisfy $\sum_{i} u_i^{2} = 1$, and put $P = I - 2uu^{T}$. Prove that if $1$ is not an eigenvalue of $Q$, then $1$ is an eigenvalue of $PQ$.
entries.name: Putnam2019B3
entries.binders: {n : ℕ} (Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (hQ : Q * Q.transpose = 1) (u : Fin n → ℝ) (hu : ∑ i, u i ^ 2 = 1) (hQ1 : ¬ ∃ v : Fin n → ℝ, v ≠ 0 ∧ Q.mulVec v = v)
entries.conclusion: ∃ v : Fin n → ℝ, v ≠ 0 ∧ Matrix.mulVec (((1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) - (2 : ℝ) • Matrix.vecMulVec u u) * Q) v = v
entries.title: Putnam 2019 B3

entries.input: Write $v \times w$ for the cross product of $v, w \in \mathbb{R}^{3}$. Prove that a finite set $S \subset \mathbb{R}^{3}$ with exactly $n$ elements satisfying $S = \{v \times w : v, w \in S\}$ exists if and only if $n = 1$ or $n = 7$.
entries.name: Putnam2022B2
entries.conclusion: (∃ S : Set (Fin 3 → ℝ), S.Finite ∧ S.ncard = n ∧ S = {x | ∃ v ∈ S, ∃ w ∈ S, crossProduct v w = x}) ↔ (n = 1 ∨ n = 7)
entries.title: Putnam 2022 B2
